title: Your First Paycheck as a Missouri CDS Caregiver (From Hired to Payday)
short_title: Your first paycheck as a CDS caregiver
description: Just hired as a CDS caregiver in Missouri? Here's every step to your first paycheck: hiring paperwork, the Family Care Safety Registry, Attendant Orientation, clocking in and out (EVV), fixing a missed clock-in, and how the Sunday to Saturday pay week turns into a Thursday payday.
end: Paid every Thursday. Questions? Call us.

parts.head: Your first paycheck as a CDS caregiver
parts.sub: From hired to payday, step by step
parts.text: You've been hired as a CDS caregiver. Congratulations! So when do you get paid, and how do you make sure that first paycheck comes through on time? I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here's every step, from hired to your first payday.

parts.head: The hiring paperwork
parts.sub: Work eligibility, W-4, direct deposit, screening consent
parts.text: First, the hiring paperwork. It's the usual employee file: a form showing you can work in the US, a W-4 for tax withholding, your direct deposit details, and your consent for the background screening. We collect it, and we tell you what's still missing before your first shift.

parts.head: Register with the state
parts.sub: Family Care Safety Registry: one-time fee, about $16
parts.text: Missouri also requires every caregiver to register with the Family Care Safety Registry. It's a one-time state fee of about sixteen dollars, and if you're already registered, you don't pay again.

parts.head: Attendant Orientation, online
parts.sub: 8 short videos, about an hour, free, no login
parts.text: Next, the Attendant Orientation. It's eight short videos, about an hour in total, free, and no login needed. You can watch on your phone, and stop and come back any time.

parts.head: Orientation at home
parts.sub: Your employer shows you how they like things done
parts.text: Your employer, the person you care for, also orients you on their home and how they like things done. It might feel formal if it's your own mom. Do it anyway. It settles questions before they turn into arguments.

parts.head: Set up clocking in (EVV)
parts.sub: The app, or the home phone. We do a practice run.
parts.text: Before your first shift, our onboarding specialist calls to set up clocking in and out, and does a practice run with you. You can use the mobile app: two taps at the start, and two at the end. Or call from the consumer's home phone, with no smartphone needed.

parts.head: Clock in and out as it happens
parts.sub: Never in advance, never after the fact
parts.text: Clock in when the shift starts, and out when it ends. Never in advance, and never after the fact. Clean clock-ins are the biggest reason a paycheck arrives without trouble.

parts.head: Use the EVV correction form
parts.sub: A Monday fix keeps Thursday's payday on time
parts.text: Forgot to clock in, or the app failed? Fill out the EVV correction form, or call us, as soon as you notice. Corrections have to be in before the weekly approval closes, so a Monday fix keeps Thursday's payday on time.

parts.head: How the money moves
parts.sub: Pay week Sun to Sat. Hours confirmed. Paid Thursday.
parts.text: Here's how the money moves. The pay week runs Sunday through Saturday. Early the next week, the person you care for confirms your recorded hours. Then you're paid that Thursday, by direct deposit or a pay card.

parts.head: $15 to $16 an hour
parts.sub: Taxes taken out. A W-2, not a 1099.
parts.text: With us, that's fifteen to sixteen dollars an hour. Taxes are taken out, and you get a W-2 at the end of the year, so there's no tax surprise.

parts.head: Only work authorized hours
parts.text: One rule that protects your paycheck: only work the hours in the plan of care. Hours that aren't authorized can't be paid. Mileage isn't paid, but driving them to an appointment counts as care time when it's in the plan.
Questions about a paycheck? Call us at 417-218-2888, Monday to Friday, nine to four, or visit caringcds.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Thanks for watching.
